summary: The abstract and main statements consistently distinguish the local conditional implication I(27) ⇒ G(80), the unconditional two-star structural theorem, and the ordinary corollary that invokes an external computational theorem. The numerical improvement is explicitly relative to two identified baselines and carries no global-priority claim. One definition repair is needed for a fully self-contained numerical statement: f(4,3) is used without specifying whether it denotes a maximum sunflower-free size or a forcing threshold, and the intersecting convention is implicit.
required_revisions: In Section 1 explicitly define intersecting as pairwise nonempty intersection for distinct members, and define f(k,r) (or at least f(4,3)) as the maximum size of an r-sunflower-free k-uniform family. State that it is the maximum-size convention, so readers using the forcing-threshold convention do not read the displayed bound off by one.

findings.statement: The numerical contribution uses f(4,3) in the abstract and Corollary 4 but never defines f; the common maximum-size and forcing-threshold conventions differ by one. The word intersecting is also left implicit.
findings.disposition: Add the explicit maximum-size and pairwise-intersection definitions near G(N) and I(N); existing numerical claims need no change if this intended convention is confirmed.

checks.method: Read the complete frozen manuscript and compared each abstract claim with Theorems 1–3, Corollary 4, and the scope paragraphs in Sections 5–7. Verified the reviewed manuscript SHA-256 against the frozen snapshot.
checks.observation: Theorem 1 explicitly requires two distinct degree-twenty centers that never co-occur and imposes no support bound. Theorem 3 retains I(27); the external theorem is invoked only in Corollary 4. The abstract preserves exactly those distinctions. The assurance label is axiom-audited and the source-rebuild limitation is disclosed.

checks.method: Traced definitions from the abstract through Section 1 and Corollary 4, checking whether every quantity in 54 ≤ f(4,3) ≤ 80 has an explicit convention.
checks.observation: G(N), the sunflower definition, distinctness and empty cores are specified, but f(4,3) is not defined. This is a definitional ambiguity rather than evidence of a mathematical error; the intended maximum-size convention is inferable but should be written.
